title: Pro-etale covers detect ordinary completed-coefficient module isomorphisms
statement: Fix ell,E [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], a nonempty qcqs scheme S [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism], and a family W:I→S.ProEt [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] of qcqs domains covering the terminal pro-etale object. On module sheaves over the completed integral coefficient sheaf on S [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], the family a↦ordinaryPull(W_a.hom) of [def-fix-qcqs-completion-ordinary-models] jointly reflects isomorphisms. Scheme, coefficient and cover-index universes are independent. This is a statement about module sheaves, not derived categories, and has no ambient immersion.

source.place: Tag 04TQ, lemma-glue-maps; proetale.tex weakly etale slice localization and coefficient restriction. Base-change the terminal cover to every test object.

proof.text: Use the completed coefficient restriction isomorphism and its finite-projection equations from completed coefficient ringed coherence. The adjunction induced by the site postcomposition/base-change adjunction sends every finite restriction map to the specified constant-section direct ring map: precompose with constant sheafification and use naturality along the site counit. Taking the compatible inverse limit and applying ordinaryCompletedRingMap_existsUnique identifies its adjunct with the exact ring map defining ordinaryPush. Mathlib SheafOfModules.pushforwardPushforwardAdj now gives the module restriction adjunction. Uniqueness of left adjoints identifies ordinaryPull with this sectionwise module restriction. These constructions keep module universe max u (t+1) and require no qcqs or nonempty hypothesis on a chart.

Generate a covering sieve from the prescribed terminal-object precover and pull it back along each test object’s structural arrow. It is contained in the sieve of objects admitting a map to some W_a; thus the family covers the top. For each object T over W_a, weakly-etale cancellation makes T.hom.left an object of W_a.left.ProEt, whose postcomposition is canonically isomorphic to T.left. The chart restriction isomorphism and evaluation therefore show that the original underlying abelian sheaf map is an isomorphism at T.left. Sheaf.isIso_of_coversTop makes the original underlying sheaf map invertible. Finally SheafOfModules.toSheaf reflects isomorphisms, giving the original module-map isomorphism. No derived-category or quotient-tower comparison is used.

theorem ordinaryCompletedCoverDetection
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (E : Type u) [Field E]
    [Algebra ℚ_[l] E] [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] E]
    (S : Scheme.{t}) [CompactSpace S] [QuasiSeparatedSpace S] [Nonempty S]
    (I : Type w) (W : I → S.ProEt)
    (hcompact : ∀ a : I, CompactSpace (W a).left)
    (hqs : ∀ a : I, QuasiSeparatedSpace (W a).left)
    (hcover : Presieve.ofArrows W
      (fun a ↦ (MorphismProperty.Over.homMk (W a).hom (Category.comp_id _) :
        W a ⟶ ProEt.mk (𝟙 S))) ∈ ProEt.precoverage S (ProEt.mk (𝟙 S))) :
    JointlyReflectIsomorphisms (fun a : I ↦ ordinaryPull l E (W a).hom)
